cucumber

An implementation of the Cucumber testing framework in R.

Introduction

The package parses Gherkin documents

Feature: Addition
  Scenario: Adding 2 integers
    When I add 1 and 1
    Then the result is 2
  Scenario: Adding integer and float
    When I add 1 and 1.1
    Then the result is 2.1
  Scenario: Adding float and float
    When I add 1.1 and 1.1
    Then the result is 2.2

and uses step definitions to run the tests

when("I add {float} and {float}", function(x, y, context) {
  context$result <- x + y
})

then("the result is {float}", function(expected, context) {
  expect_equal(context$result, expected)
})

The building blocks of the cucumber tests are Features and Scenarios.

  • Each Feature will be treated as a separate context – their results will be reported as if they were test-*.R files, e.g. 'test-Feature: Addition.R'.
  • Each Scenario is equivalent to a testthat::test_that or testthat::it case. You get feedback on each Scenario separately. Only if all steps in a scenario are successful, the scenario is considered successful.

Run the tests with cucumber::test(). By default it uses the CucumberProgressReporter, which prints a line for each feature with its scenarios counted by status:

withr::with_dir(pass_dir, {
  cucumber::test(filter = "addition")
})
  |  F  P  U  S  OK | Feature
v |               3 | Addition

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
  3 scenarios (3 passed)
  6 steps (6 passed)
  0m00.100s (executing steps: 0m00.100s)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When a step fails, the reporter shows which step broke and why as soon as its scenario finishes, and again in the summary at the end:

withr::with_dir(fail_dir, {
  cucumber::test(filter = "addition")
})
  |  F  P  U  S  OK | Feature

Feature: Addition
  Scenario: Adding integer and float
    v When I add 1 and 1.1
    x Then the result is 5
    Error: 
      Step "the result is 5" failed
      i Feature: addition.feature:7
      i Scenario: Adding integer and float
      i Step defined at: setup-steps-addition.R:5
      Expected `context$result` to equal `expected`.
      Differences:
        `actual`: 2.1
      `expected`: 5.0

Feature: Addition
  Scenario: Adding float and float
    v When I add 1.1 and 1.1
    x Then the result is 5
    Error: 
      Step "the result is 5" failed
      i Feature: addition.feature:10
      i Scenario: Adding float and float
      i Step defined at: setup-steps-addition.R:5
      Expected `context$result` to equal `expected`.
      Differences:
        `actual`: 2.2
      `expected`: 5.0
x |  2            1 | Addition

Failures:

1) Scenario: Adding integer and float # addition.feature:5
    v When I add 1 and 1.1
    x Then the result is 5
    Error: 
      Step "the result is 5" failed
      i Feature: addition.feature:7
      i Scenario: Adding integer and float
      i Step defined at: setup-steps-addition.R:5
      Expected `context$result` to equal `expected`.
      Differences:
        `actual`: 2.1
      `expected`: 5.0

2) Scenario: Adding float and float # addition.feature:8
    v When I add 1.1 and 1.1
    x Then the result is 5
    Error: 
      Step "the result is 5" failed
      i Feature: addition.feature:10
      i Scenario: Adding float and float
      i Step defined at: setup-steps-addition.R:5
      Expected `context$result` to equal `expected`.
      Differences:
        `actual`: 2.2
      `expected`: 5.0

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
  3 scenarios (2 failed, 1 passed)
  6 steps (2 failed, 4 passed)
  0m00.100s (executing steps: 0m00.100s)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Error:
! Test failures.

To see every step as it runs, use CucumberPrettyReporter. CucumberDotsReporter, CucumberProgressBarReporter and CucumberSummaryReporter.

withr::with_dir(pass_dir, {
  cucumber::test(filter = "addition", reporter = cucumber::CucumberPrettyReporter$new())
})
Feature: Addition
  Scenario: Adding 2 integers
    v When I add 1 and 1
    v Then the result is 2
  Scenario: Adding integer and float
    v When I add 1 and 1.1
    v Then the result is 2.1
  Scenario: Adding float and float
    v When I add 1.1 and 1.1
    v Then the result is 2.2


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Summary
  3 scenarios (3 passed)
  6 steps (6 passed)
  0m00.100s (executing steps: 0m00.100s)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Put your acceptance tests in a directory separate to your unit tests:

tests/
├── acceptance/
│   ├── setup-steps_1.R
│   ├── setup-steps_2.R
│   ├── feature_1.feature
│   ├── feature_2.feature
├── testthat/
│   ├── test-unit_test_1.R
│   ├── test-unit_test_2.R

or alongside your unit tests:

tests/
├── testthat/
│   ├── test-cucumber.R
│   ├── test-unit_test_1.R
│   ├── test-unit_test_2.R
│   ├── setup-steps_1.R
│   ├── setup-steps_2.R
│   ├── feature_1.feature
│   ├── feature_2.feature

Examples

See the examples directory to help you get started.

Reports

Write the official Cucumber HTML report of a run with CucumberHtmlReporter, and its JUnit XML report with CucumberJunitReporter. Steps and hooks attach screenshots and logs to it, like those of a failing shinytest2 scenario: see the Reports article and its report.

Scenarios as documentation

Feature files already say how your package behaves, so let them document it. Tag the scenarios that illustrate a function with @rd

Feature: Basket
  A basket holds the items a customer wants to buy.

  @rd
  Scenario: Add an item
    Given an empty basket
    When I add 1 item
    Then the basket has 1 item

  Scenario: Remove an item from an empty basket
    Given an empty basket
    When I remove 1 item
    Then the basket is empty

and put them in its help page with features_rd():

#' Add items to a basket
#' @eval cucumber::features_rd(features = "basket.feature")
#' @export
add <- function(basket, n) basket + n

devtools::document() adds a Behavior section to ?add with the feature’s description and the tagged scenarios:

Add items to a basket

Description:

     Add items to a basket

Usage:

     add(basket, n)
     
Behavior:

     Feature: Basket
       A basket holds the items a customer wants to buy.
     
       Scenario: Add an item
         Given an empty basket
         When I add 1 item
         Then the basket has 1 item
     
     Source: 'tests/acceptance/basket.feature'

The help pages of this package are written this way, see ?hook or ?test: the scenarios that test cucumber explain it, and stay true because they run.

How it works

The .feature files are parsed and matched against step definitions.

Step functions are defined using:

  • description: a cucumber expression.
  • and an implementation function. It must have the parameters that will be matched in the description and a context parameter - an environment for managing state between steps.

Text in a description is matched literally, except for:

  • {int} and other parameter types, whose values are passed to the implementation,
  • (s) – optional text: "I have {int} cucumber(s)" matches both I have 1 cucumber and I have 2 cucumbers,
  • a/b – alternative words: "I press the Enter/Return key" matches either word.

To match (, { or / literally, escape them with a backslash, e.g. "a\\/b". An invalid expression, like "I visit /about", is an error.

A description that starts with ^, ends with $ or is surrounded by / is a regular expression instead, e.g. "^I have (\\d+) cucumbers?$". Each capture group is passed to the implementation.

Each step parsed from the .feature files must match exactly one step definition. A step that matches none is undefined: its scenario fails, the run goes on, and a ready-to-paste snippet is shown. A step that matches more than one is ambiguous: its scenario fails with an error listing every matching definition.

Parameter types

Step implementations receive data from the .feature files as parameters. The values are detected via regular expressions and cast with a transformer function.

The following parameter types are available by default:

Parameter Type Description
{int} Matches integers, for example 71 or -19. Converts value with as.integer.
float Matches floats, for example 3.6, .8, -9.2 or 1.5E3, and integers like 12. Converts value with as.double.
{word} Matches words without whitespace, for example banana or foo-bar (but not banana split).
{string} Matches single-quoted or double-quoted strings, for example “banana split” or ‘banana split’ (but not banana split). Only the text between the quotes will be extracted, with escaped quotes unescaped.
{} Matches anything. Passes the matched text as is.

See cucumber::define_parameter_type() how to define your own parameter types.

Installation

To install the stable version from CRAN:

install.packages("cucumber")
